collocations: restrain from, restrain spending, restrain growth, restrain oneself, restrain inflation
example: To restrain rising inflation, the central bank decided to increase interest rates by 0.5 percentage points.

meaning: 硬直した、厳格な、融通の利かない
meaningEn: stiff, inflexible, or strictly enforced
collocations: rigid rules, rigid structure, rigid adherence, rigid thinking, rigid control
example: The company's rigid hierarchy often prevented employees from proposing innovative solutions.

meaningEn: lower in rank or position; a person under the authority of another
collocations: subordinate role, subordinate staff, subordinate clause, subordinate position, subordinate to
example: In many organisations, managers are expected to delegate tasks to their subordinates to improve efficiency.

meaning: 違反する、侵害する、乱す
meaningEn: to break a rule, law, or agreement; to disturb or disrespect something
collocations: violate a law, violate an agreement, violate rights, violate privacy, violate regulations
example: If a country continues to violate international trade agreements, it may face severe economic sanctions.

meaningEn: Although, even though (conjunction)
collocations: albeit with, albeit in, albeit at, albeit slowly, albeit briefly

meaningEn: To gather together or put parts together
collocations: assemble a team, assemble the parts, assemble evidence, assemble quickly, assemble a group
example: The committee will assemble next week to discuss the new proposal.

meaningEn: To collect information from various sources and arrange it
collocations: compile a list, compile data, compile a report, compile information, compile statistics
example: The researchers compiled data from over 100 studies to draw their conclusions.

meaning: 間近に迫った、今後発表される、協力的な
meaningEn: about to happen or appear; willing to give information or help
collocations: forthcoming event, forthcoming publication, forthcoming election, forthcoming release, forthcoming meeting
example: The government has not been forthcoming with detailed data regarding the environmental impact of the new policy.

meaningEn: The quality of being honest and having strong moral principles
collocations: personal integrity, academic integrity, integrity of, maintain integrity, moral integrity
example: The company values integrity above all other qualities in its employees.

meaningEn: Belonging naturally to something; essential and inherent.
collocations: intrinsic value, intrinsic to, intrinsic quality, intrinsic motivation, intrinsic nature
example: Education has intrinsic value beyond its economic benefits.

meaning: （権利・規則などを）発動する、呼び起こす、引用する
meaningEn: to call upon a law, authority, or idea; to evoke or cite as support
synonyms: cite, call upon, appeal to, summon, evoke
collocations: invoke a law, invoke a clause, invoke a right, invoke a precedent, invoke a memory

meaningEn: An imposed tax or fee
collocations: impose a levy, levy a tax, levy on imports, carbon levy, levy fine

meaningEn: in spite of; nevertheless; however
collocations: notwithstanding the fact, notwithstanding the risks, notwithstanding the opposition, notwithstanding the evidence, notwithstanding the delay

meaningEn: Continuing or still in progress
synonyms: continuing, current, developing, in progress, persistent
collocations: ongoing project, ongoing process, ongoing issue, ongoing support, ongoing research

meaningEn: To continue to exist or happen; to continue doing something despite difficulty.
collocations: persist in, persist despite, persist over time, problem persists, persist with

meaning: 気乗りしないこと、不本意、ためらい
meaningEn: unwillingness or hesitation to do something
collocations: reluctance to change, show reluctance, overcome reluctance, initial reluctance, growing reluctance

meaning: いわゆる、自称の、名ばかりの
